kitDescription: Marciana is a pure healer whose personal damage comes entirely from her shotgun. Whenever she fires the last bullet of a magazine, all allies regenerate a portion of her attack damage as health over 3 seconds, and the two allies with the highest final ATK additionally receive increased incoming healing for 3 seconds. When she uses her Burst Skill, the whole team instantly recovers health equal to a share of her own Max HP. Her Burst Skill also sets up a storage effect that banks any excess healing she receives (up to a cap based on her Max HP) for 10 seconds, and raises all allies' DEF based on her own DEF for 10 seconds. Nothing in her kit deals damage or modifies her weapon.

Tick count is a convention both sides adopted and S2b prescribed; heal magnitude is unrepresentable (no HP pool) and is documented, not invented. Driver M2 counterfactual (ticks:1) discriminates.

verdictRationale: No real gotchas: all 5 kit lines are FAITHFUL (3) or DOCUMENTED_GAP (2), and every trap S2b pre-registered was avoided by both the driver and the blind override-writer — burstCast-not-fullBurstEnter on skill2/burst (trap #1), both heals modeled as recovery events rather than silently dropped (#2), the S1 HoT kept at ticks:3 rather than collapsed to one instant event (#3), and Storage kept unmodeled-verbatim instead of being encoded as a shield (#4). The S5 RED (6 failures) is entirely recon error: 4 assertions observe a 'heal'/'recovery' SimEvent kind the engine provably never emits (the log's only kinds are buffApply/burstCast/damage/fullBurstEnd/fullBurstStart/reload/shot; heals are observable only via consumer buffApply, which the driver test does correctly via asuka's atkPct 96.98), and the other 2 stem from the blind fixture's co-B2 contention (crown wins every Burst-II slot: marciana burstCast 0, crown 10), which fails the blind test's own non-vacuity gate. Convergence evidence is strong despite the RED: the cross-family S6 override is functionally identical to the driver's (same triggers, targets, ticks, defPct value/duration, same two verbatim unmodeled lines, same Storage-NOT-shield and caster-DEF caveats), and the 15 S5 passes independently confirm the inertness envelope, target sets, duration bound, and no-damage fabrication. Fire-rate check passes: heals fire at prose cadence (70 consumer firings = 3x21 last-bullets + 8 bursts; defPct 24 = 8x3 at 600-frame expiry). Driver discrimination holds via live counterfactuals (ticks:1 collapse, defAsDamage movement, byte-exact noDef equality). Same-model residual for the owner to spot-check: the ticks:3/intervalSec:1 reading of 'over 3 sec' is a shared convention (prescribed by S2b, adopted by driver and S6 alike) rather than a measured tick cadence — it directly scales how often on-recovery consumers refresh, so a real HoT that ticks differently (e.g. a single application with a 3s duration tag) would over-credit consumers 3x; this is the one number a frame-read of a recovery-consumer's refresh cadence could pin, and it is the only residual standing between this encoding and full measurement-tier confidence.
